quoted_clause: When a GPU is idle waiting, we reach for DP (more work per GPU)
observed: Data parallelism does not give an idle GPU more work. It adds independent replicas, each with its own model copy and its own request stream. If a single GPU is idle because arrivals are insufficient, DP does not raise that GPU's utilization; it adds another underutilized GPU. DP is a response to aggregate demand exceeding one replica's goodput, not to a single GPU being idle.
correction: Replace with: 'When aggregate demand exceeds one replica's goodput, add DP replicas. When a single GPU is idle because the batch or arrival stream is too small, increase batching/admission or reduce over-provisioning; DP does not fill that GPU.'
acceptance_test: A reader can explain why DP does not increase utilization of an already-idle GPU and can name the correct levers for low arrival rate versus insufficient aggregate capacity.
verdict_evidence: ch10 L36 'When a GPU is idle waiting, we reach for DP (more work per GPU)' conflicts with L17 ('Inference: independent replicas each serve a disjoint set of requests') and L30 ('Data parallel replicates the whole model and splits the batch') — replication adds capacity, and splitting the batch gives each GPU less work, not more.
fix_instruction: Replace with 'When aggregate demand exceeds one replica's goodput, add DP replicas; when a single GPU is idle for lack of arrivals or batch, the fix is batching/admission or less over-provisioning — DP does not fill that GPU.'

quoted_clause: for N=8 the per-rank send volume is (N-1)/N × 280 ≈ 245 GB and the send-plus-receive total is 1.75 × 280 ≈ 490 GB ... At 25 GB/s (single 200Gb/s link) that is 245 / 25 ≈ 9.8 s per step ... At the H100 NVLink directional peak of 450 GB/s, the same ideal ring estimate is 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s
observed: The 280 GB FP32 gradient case reuses the 140 GB FP16 gradient traffic numbers from Chapter 9. For a ring all-reduce with M=280 GB and N=8, the total per-rank send volume is 2*(N-1)/N*M = 490 GB, not 245 GB; the per-rank receive volume is also 490 GB, and send-plus-receive is 980 GB, not 490 GB.
correction: Either state that 245 GB is the one-phase send volume and give the full two-phase send volume as 490 GB with times 19.6 s at 25 GB/s and ≈1.09 s at 450 GB/s, or explicitly keep the 140 GB FP16 example for the 9.8 s / 0.54 s numbers. Do not mix 280 GB logical size with 140 GB traffic arithmetic.
acceptance_test: Recompute from M=280 GB, N=8: printed per-rank total send, total receive, send-plus-receive, and both bandwidth times must match 490 GB, 490 GB, 980 GB, 19.6 s, and ≈1.09 s respectively, or the text must clearly label 245 GB as one-phase only and use 490 GB for total send time.
verdict_evidence: ch10: 'a ring all-reduce moves 2(N-1)/N times the per-rank gradient through each rank, so for N=8 the per-rank send volume is (N-1)/N × 280 ≈ 245 GB ... At 25 GB/s that is 245 / 25 ≈ 9.8 s ... 245/450 ≈ 0.54 s'. 2×7/8×280 = 490 GB per rank (send+receive 980), so the times are 19.6 s and 1.09 s; 245 GB and 9.8 s/0.54 s are exactly ch9's M=140 GB figures (ch9: 'each phase sends (N-1)M/N=122.5 GB per rank ... therefore sends 245 GB and receives another 245 GB per rank').
fix_instruction: Restate at M=280: two phases × 245 GB = 490 GB sent per rank (490 GB received), so T ≈ 490/25 ≈ 19.6 s on a 200 Gb/s link and 490/450 ≈ 1.09 s at the NVLink directional peak; label 490 GB as the send volume (send+receive = 980 GB), not 'the send-plus-receive total'.

quoted_clause: When a GPU is idle waiting, we reach for DP (more work per GPU); CP addresses long-sequence/KV capacity, not idle-fill.
observed: DP does not make an idle single GPU do more work; it adds independent replicas or increases total batch across devices. If a GPU is idle because arrivals are low, DP does not fill that GPU. If it is idle because the batch is small, the direct levers are batch size, microbatching, or continuous batching, not necessarily DP.
correction: Reword to: "When aggregate throughput is limited by batch size and the model fits, DP adds replicas/total batch; it is not a per-GPU idle-fill mechanism."
acceptance_test: A reader should not infer that DP fills an underloaded single GPU.
verdict_evidence: Mental model: 'When a GPU is *idle* waiting, we reach for DP (more work per GPU)' — DP replicates the model and splits the batch (ch10: 'training: replicates all weights on every GPU, feeds each a different batch'; inference: 'independent replicas each serve a disjoint set of requests'), so it adds devices/work in parallel; it does not put more work on an idle device, and if arrivals are low it cannot fill one.
fix_instruction: Reword: 'When aggregate throughput, not memory, is the limit — the data corner is what is starved — we reach for DP (more replicas, each with its own batch). DP does not create work for an idle GPU; if the device is idle for lack of arrivals, DP makes it idler.'
